bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Persistent Chinese dumping in aroma ingredients; oversupply in Indian camphor market; prolonged Mahad ramp-up delays; margin compression if pricing doesn't recover; inventory liquidity risk
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on volume growth and long-term margin recovery; transparent about short-term pain from Mahad and pricing; dismissive of anti-dumping petition for camphor; focused on operational efficiency and customer retention

bull_bear.body: Mahad plant is EBITDA negative now but product is already being sold; hydrogenation plant is EBITDA positive and integrated; camphor imports are natural (not synthetic), so not direct competition; trading division is growing but not segmented in reporting
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Net Debt-to-Equity Ratio improved to 0.56x as of June 30, 2026, reflecting the Company's continued focus on disciplined capital allocation, prudent financial management and strengthening its balance sheet."
- Deck's Net D/E (x) chart shows 0.30 (FY24), 0.51 (FY25), 0.58 (FY26) — i.e. the June-2026 0.56x is an improvement off the FY26 level.
- The deck discloses no dividend policy, buyback, or reinvestment framework.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Full integration across the value chain - from molecule synthesis and complex chemistry to formulation, manufacturing and global customer delivery - making the Company a long-term supply partner to FMCG, pharmaceutical and perfumery brands
- Four manufacturing locations across three Indian states enabling stringent quality control, efficient scale-up and supply chain reliability
- Depth of chemistry: over 100 aroma ingredients manufactured using 26 complex chemistries
- Bareilly is among the few facilities globally holding USFDA and WHO-GMP accreditations for pharmaceutical-grade camphor
- Owned heritage retail camphor brands Saraswati (registered 1967) and 3 Pine, which contribute over 60% of OAL's camphor production and give direct domestic consumer presence
- Generational fragrance customer relationships spanning multiple decades
- In-house access to aroma ingredients (backward integration) supporting the fragrance division
- Recognised by customers - received the Global Supplier Excellence Award from Procter & Gamble for 2023
- Long operating history - uninterrupted operations since 1955, camphor manufacturing at Bareilly since 1964
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Buyer's market and limited pricing power in aroma ingredients — Global aroma ingredient markets remained buyer-led, limiting pricing power and keeping end-product realisations subdued; in a buyers' market, customer resistance to price increases can delay full recovery of raw material cost inflation.
- Chinese capacity pressure and dumping in non-tariff markets — Capacities built by Chinese players continued to flow into non-tariff markets including India, Southeast Asia and parts of Europe, creating intense pricing pressure. OAL responded by prioritising volume leadership, market share and customer retention over short-term margins and by running a CPR (process re-engineering) programme to structurally reduce costs.
- Domestic camphor overcapacity and product concentration in commodity B2B camphor — The Indian camphor market remained impacted by supply exceeding demand due to substantial domestic capacity additions, and natural camphor imports from China continued to influence pricing; exposure to highly competitive B2B commodity camphor meant low pricing power and margin compression. OAL internalised its heritage brands (Saraswati, 3 Pine, Bhimseni), shifting 60% of the camphor business into the formulated B2C space.
- Input cost inflation and currency depreciation — Gum turpentine, crude sulphate turpentine and alpha-pinene prices remained elevated while crude-based raw materials were volatile and difficult to source; Rupee depreciation affected the imported portion of the raw material basket across all three divisions. OAL secured feedstock ahead of festive production cycles and held higher inventory when prices were perceived to be lowest.
- Geopolitical and trade risk / tariff exposure of the export book — Uncertainty over North American tariffs (which briefly reached 50% for certain categories) and global trade instability impacted export volumes and inventory building by U.S. customers; OAL evaluated alternate market channels and, following a new trade deal, is leveraging a restored 20% tariff advantage over Chinese competitors.
- Execution and margin drag from the Mahad greenfield ramp-up — Early-stage ramp-up of the Mahad facility, alongside soft aroma ingredient pricing and buyer-market conditions, weighed on profitability; management's priority is to stabilise Mahad and accelerate its commercial ramp-up.
- Financial leverage from rapid, debt-funded asset creation — Rapid asset creation and debt-funded expansion could strain the balance sheet during a soft pricing environment; OAL states it followed a conservative capital structure with net debt-to-equity kept at 0.60x to 0.65x.
- Seasonality and cautious discretionary consumer demand — Significant demand fluctuations between quarters (Q1 and Q3 traditionally softer than the festive peak in Q2) can create revenue and cash-flow volatility, while broader macroeconomic uncertainty led to cautious consumer behaviour with fragrances and flavours still perceived at the margin as discretionary. A diversified mix across fragrances, aroma ingredients and camphor is the stated cushion.
- Environmental compliance - waste, water and wastewater management — BRSR flags waste management compliance and water/wastewater management as material risks with negative financial implications: operations generate hazardous and non-hazardous waste and involve significant water usage, where inadequate handling risks environmental harm, regulatory non-compliance and escalating costs.
- Responsible supply chain and human rights — BRSR identifies both as material risks - supply disruptions or unethical sourcing can affect production and reputation, and human rights violations can hit employee morale, reputation, legal exposure and stakeholder relationships.

outlook.body:
- Build long-term capabilities rather than chase short-term opportunities, relying on the integrated model spanning fragrance creation, specialty aroma ingredients and terpene chemistry
- Accelerate the commercial ramp-up of the Mahad greenfield facility through customer qualification, commercial shipments and participation in global sourcing programmes
- Consolidate the manufacturing investments made over the past few years and maximise the potential of existing assets before pursuing further expansion
- Drive volume growth and strengthen market position, and progressively improve margins through internal efficiency and process improvement initiatives
- Improve operating leverage, enhance manufacturing efficiencies and optimise product mix to progressively restore margins as new capacities mature
- Strengthen consumer camphor brands Saraswati and 3 Pine, deepen customer relationships and expand distribution instead of responding to overcapacity with short-term price measures
- Deepen relationships with existing fragrance customers while expanding presence across new domestic and international markets, supported by backward integration
- Maintain disciplined capital allocation - invest patiently in high-quality assets, keep the balance sheet healthy and preserve financial flexibility
- Continue investing in technology, innovation, operational excellence and people, with the objective of building an organisation globally respected for technology, manufacturing excellence, innovation and responsible business practices
- Embed sustainability - responsible manufacturing, resource efficiency, environmental stewardship, governance and community development - into the way business is conducted
- Governance disclosures express capital allocation mainly through the dividend decision: the Board, at its meeting held on 20th May, 2026, recommended a final dividend of Rs 0.50 per equity share (10% of the Rs 5 face value) for the financial year ended 31st March, 2026, to be declared by members at the 54th AGM and paid out of the profits of the Company to eligible members, with tax deducted at source since dividends are taxable in shareholders' hands. Beyond this, the Company frames governance as a cornerstone of long-term value creation and states no separate payout, buyback or reinvestment policy in these sections.
- All OAL facilities are ISO 14001:2015 certified for environmental management, with pollution control systems and compliance processes integrated across manufacturing units
- ISO 45001:2018 certification for occupational health and safety management across sites, supported by PPE provision, regular training, structured process control and incident review systems
- ISO 9001:2015 certification for quality management across sites
- Dedicated wastewater treatment plants with advanced systems so that all wastewater is treated and discharged in compliance with prescribed regulatory standards
- Robust waste management protocols including strict segregation and engagement with authorised vendors for hazardous waste disposal, plus proactive identification of circularity opportunities
- Decarbonisation identified as a material sustainability issue and an opportunity, since manufacturing operations generate emissions that contribute to climate change
- Human rights upheld through established policies, regular training and awareness programmes and a robust whistleblower mechanism
- Responsible supply chain maintained through comprehensive pre-onboarding assessments and ongoing vendor quality evaluations
- Emphasis on responsible manufacturing, compliance, pollution control, water management, process safety, material handling, emissions and employee health for chemical operations
- Diversity and inclusion and employee wellbeing identified as material opportunities; the Company reports stable and cordial industrial relations across all facilities and employed 768 individuals as of 31st March 2026
- Community engagement and social impact identified as a material opportunity, with commitment to positive environmental and socio-economic development
- Corporate governance identified as a material opportunity - fostering transparency, mitigating conflicts of interest and ensuring regulatory compliance
- BRSR disclosures for FY 2025-26 are made on a standalone basis and are not externally assured (assurance provider and type of assurance both stated as NA)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: OAL describes FY 2025-26 as a year of stabilising recent capacity additions rather than adding new ones, with integrated manufacturing across four sites - Bareilly, Vadodara, Ambernath and Mahad. The Mahad greenfield facility, built on land acquired at Mahad, Maharashtra for a new aroma chemicals plant, continued through its ramp-up and stabilisation phase: it completed sampling cycles with global customers, commenced commercial shipments and qualified to participate in major global RFQs for the second half of 2026, while currently carrying an estimated 1% to 1.5% impact on consolidated EBITDA margins. Mahad also commenced production of Evermoss, a specialty aroma product. At Vadodara, the hydrogenation facility is integrated into the wider Vadodara product chain, leading to increased output of aroma ingredients, following earlier commissioning of specialty aroma chemical facilities and a dedicated Astromusk plant at the site. Bareilly, the long-standing camphor and terpene chemicals site (India's first synthetic camphor plant, using DuPont US technology), runs at around 85-90% capacity, is relevant for US FDA and WHO-GMP-certified camphor, and had its terpene chemicals plant capacity expanded. The Ambernath flavour and fragrance compounding plant operates at one shift, with the ability to expand capacity by adding shifts. Company-wide, production volumes increased 5% year-on-year and sales volumes grew 9%. Management's stated priority is to convert these recent investments into higher utilisation, customer approvals and volume growth, consolidating existing assets rather than pursuing fresh expansion, while continuing to expand the retail B2C footprint of the internalised heritage camphor brands Saraswati and 3 Pine.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Premiumisation across personal care, home care and fine fragrances continues to create opportunities for differentiated fragrance solutions
- Growth of rural FMCG consumption is expanding the reach of personal care and spiritual products across Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets, supporting the Fragrances & Flavours and Camphor businesses
- Products reached customers across 27 States and Union Territories, strengthening domestic presence
- International business contributed approximately 33.38% of total revenue, with products reaching more than 35 countries across five continents
- Approximately three-fourths of the Specialty Aroma Ingredients division's production serves international markets
- North America, which operated under tariff uncertainty for much of the year, began showing signs of recovery as policy clarity improved in the latter months of FY 2025-26
- South-East Asia and the Middle East remain important growth markets, while Europe remained resilient despite a challenging environment for specialty ingredients
- Specialty Aroma Ingredients operated amid global overcapacity and sustained pricing pressure
- Camphor and terpene chemicals faced a challenging domestic environment where industry capacity exceeded demand
- The second half of the year saw meaningful inflation in several fragrance raw materials, partly offset by cost management, process optimisation and backward integration
- Profitability during the year reflected raw material inflation, currency movements and the planned costs of the Mahad commercial ramp-up, which management describes as investments in the future rather than structural concerns
- For chemical companies serving consumer, FMCG, personal care, home care and export end-markets, the environment is expected to remain influenced by currency movements, tariff developments and volatility in raw-material and energy costs
- Sector demand is expected to grow in a measured manner backed by high-performance applications, while producers face pressure from energy and raw material costs, Chinese capacity in select chains, tariffs and customer inventory cycles
- India's near-term outlook is driven by resilient consumption, sustained public capital expenditure and improving private investment intentions, with sector performance shaped by consumer staples, personal and home care, processed foods, wellness and faith-linked consumption
- Customers with strong proximity, process efficiency and application capabilities are better placed to protect volumes and margins in soft pricing environments
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Record sales volume growth (30% QoQ) driven by market share gains, but EBITDA margin collapsed to 6.34% due to pricing pressure from Chinese dumping and Mahad plant ramp-up drag; margins expected to recover as Mahad reaches 60%+ utilization and cost optimization matures.
